system.name: RoCE BALBOA
system.one_liner: an open, modular RDMA/RoCEv2 offload engine for data-center SmartNICs with exchangeable slots for on-datapath and parallel-path service enhancements

components.name: QPN
components.role: queue-pair number field in the per-QP state table

components.name: PSN-Head/Tail
components.role: packet-sequence-number head/tail fields tracking the per-QP outstanding packet window

components.name: Request-Buffer
components.role: queues incoming RDMA requests when the per-QP packet budget is exhausted

components.name: HBM-Channel
components.role: HBM memory channel that stores retransmission data and commands

components.name: Bitmasking-Stage
components.role: masks input bits before CRC computation

components.name: CRC512
components.role: computes a CRC over a 512-bit chunk of the data beat

components.name: CRC320
components.role: computes a CRC over a 320-bit chunk of the data beat

components.name: CRC32_0
components.role: one of 16 parallel 32-bit CRC lanes (CRC32_0 ... CRC32_15) combined to build the final ICRC

components.name: CRC Insertion & Beat Creation
components.role: inserts the computed CRC into the packet and (re)creates the output data beat

flows.what: per-QP packet budget decreased when a new request is sent
per-QP packet budget increased upon receipt of an RDMA ACK, allowing a queued request to be forwarded

summary: This figure isolates three of BALBOA's building blocks named in the caption: ACK-clocked flow control, retransmission logic, and the ICRC pipeline. In the flow-control panel, incoming RDMA requests are either forwarded to the packet-processing pipeline or queued in a Request-Buffer once a per-QP packet budget (tracked via QPN and PSN-Head/Tail state) is exhausted; the budget is decremented on new requests and incremented on received ACKs. The retransmission panel shows an HBM-Channel handling RDMA write/read-response data and data-fetch/delivery commands for replaying lost packets from HBM. The ICRC panel shows a bitmasking stage feeding parallel CRC512, CRC320 and sixteen CRC32 lanes whose results are combined in a final CRC-insertion-and-beat-creation stage. The three panels are drawn as independent block diagrams rather than one connected pipeline.

notes: layout-proposal: independent-building-block-panels — three self-contained mini block-diagrams (flow control, retransmission, CRC) placed side by side without a shared dataflow between them. Panels 2 (retransmission) and 3 (ICRC) are described mainly from their figure labels since the body-text passages available focus on panel 1 (flow control).
